title: Gaia's promise to detect compact-object binaries II: Predictions for dormant neutron star binaries in DR4 and beyond
comment: 28 pages, 13 figures, 1 table, submitted to the Astrophysical Journal; comments welcome
summary: With the fourth data release (DR4) from Gaia imminent, we predict neutron star (NS) binaries with luminous companions (LCs) expected to be detectable in DR4 and the final data release (DR5). We create realistic synthetic populations of NS--LC binaries in the Milky Way using COSMIC, assuming (a) observationally motivated initial distributions of binary properties, (b) metallicity and location dependent star formation history of the MW adopted from the FIRE-2 galaxy m12i, and (c) all relevant binary interaction physics, with the rapid and delayed supernova prescriptions. We estimate the detectable NS--LC population using an approximate Gaia\ selection function based on projected orbital size of the LC as well as gaiamock, which emulates Gaia's multi-epoch astrometry and orbit-fitting pipeline- both after taking into account extinction and reddening. Across supernova models and statistical fluctuations, the former (gaiamock) pipeline predicts $\sim14$--$29$ ($\sim1$--$8$), $4500$--$4700$ ($100$--$110$), and $4800$--$5000$ ($300$--$380$) detectable NS--LC binaries in DR3, DR4, and DR5, respectively. While the orbital-size based pipeline brackets the DR3 yield of NS--LC candidates, the gaiamock prediction falls short, suggesting uncertainties in the modeled binary evolution or contributions from other formation channels. DR4 is expected to directly shed light on the the relative importance of detectable NS--LC binaries from isolated binary evolution vis a vis other channels such as dynamical formation. Interestingly, our models suggest that future releases will also include $22^{+7}_{-5}\ (13^{+5}_{-4})$ and $124^{+14}_{-15}\ (53^{+10}_{-6})$ gaiamock-detectable pulsar--MS binaries in DR4 and DR5, respectively, for the rapid (delayed) model, which are prime targets for radio follow-up.

AI.tldr: This paper predicts the number of Gaia-detectable neutron star binaries with luminous companions in future data releases (DR4, DR5), using COSMIC binary population synthesis with FIRE-2-informed star formation history and two Gaia detection pipelines, yielding forecasts of several thousand detectable systems and a subset of pulsar–main-sequence binaries suited to radio follow-up.
AI.motivation: With Gaia DR4 imminent, there is a need to forecast how many neutron star binaries with luminous companions can be detected, and to understand what these yields imply about binary evolution and formation channels (isolated binary evolution versus dynamical formation). Such predictions guide target selection and interpretation of future Gaia releases.
AI.method: The authors build synthetic Milky Way populations of NS–LC binaries using COSMIC, adopting observationally motivated initial binary distributions, a metallicity- and location-dependent star formation history from the FIRE-2 m12i simulation, full binary interaction physics, and rapid/delayed supernova prescriptions. Detectability is estimated with two pipelines: an approximate selection function based on the projected orbital size of the luminous companion, and gaiamock, which emulates Gaia multi-epoch astrometry and orbit fitting; both account for extinction and reddening.
AI.result: Across supernova models and statistical fluctuations, the orbital-size pipeline predicts ~14–29, 4500–4700, and 4800–5000 detectable NS–LC binaries in DR3, DR4, and DR5, respectively, while gaiamock predicts ~1–8, 100–110, and 300–380. The orbital-size pipeline brackets the DR3 candidate yield, whereas gaiamock underpredicts it, pointing to uncertainties in binary evolution modeling or additional formation channels. The models also predict 22(+7/−5) (13(+5/−4)) and 124(+14/−15) (53(+10/−6)) gaiamock-detectable pulsar–MS binaries in DR4 and DR5 for the rapid (delayed) model.
AI.conclusion: Gaia DR4/DR5 should detect thousands (orbital-size) or hundreds (gaiamock) of NS–LC binaries, enabling assessment of the relative contribution of isolated binary evolution versus dynamical channels. The DR3 underprediction by gaiamock highlights modeling uncertainties. Future releases should also yield a population of pulsar–main-sequence binaries that are prime targets for radio follow-up.

title: Mining the time axis with TRON. IV. MeerKAT detects a radio burst from a nearby M~dwarf
summary: We report the detection of a minute-timescale, highly circularly polarised ($\sim100\%$) radio burst from an active M dwarf (spectral type M1Ve), PM J14111$-$6155, located 19.6 pc from the Sun. Identified in the 1.28 GHz SMGPS using 8-second integrations from the TRON-pipeline, the burst peaked at 7.7 mJy. Visibility-based dynamic spectra reveal a drifting, band-limited emission feature ($\sim$300 MHz FWHM) with a maximum cut-off near 1.65 GHz, associated with electron cyclotron maser instability (ECMI), implying the existence of large-scale magnetic topologies ($B_* \approx 0.59$ kG). A non-detection ($3σ$ upper limit) four hours later points to intermittent or rotationally modulated beamed emission. An analysis of both TESS and ground-based survey data failed to recover an unambiguous rotational period for the optical counterpart. Follow-up SALT spectroscopy confirms its active chromospheric state, exhibiting prominent emission in the Ca {\sc ii} infrared triplet, Balmer lines, and persistent double-peaked H$α$ emission ($44.6\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ peak separation) attributable to optically thick self-absorption. This discovery demonstrates that the coordinated use of time-series optical photometry, high-resolution spectroscopy, and high-cadence spectropolarimetric radio imaging enables direct probing of coherent radio emission from the magnetically active atmospheres of nearby M dwarfs.

AI.tldr: Detection of a minutes-timescale, highly circularly polarized (~100%) 1.28 GHz radio burst from nearby active M dwarf PM J14111−6155, attributed to electron cyclotron maser instability implying a ~0.59 kG magnetic field.
AI.motivation: Probe coherent radio emission from magnetically active atmospheres of nearby M dwarfs by combining high-cadence spectropolarimetric radio imaging with optical photometry and spectroscopy, addressing the origin of stellar radio bursts and magnetic topology.
AI.method: 1.28 GHz SMGPS observations with 8-s integrations via the TRON pipeline; visibility-based dynamic spectra analysis; TESS and ground-based photometry for period recovery; SALT high-resolution spectroscopy (Ca II IRT, Balmer lines, Hα).
AI.result: Burst peak 7.7 mJy; drifting band-limited feature (~300 MHz FWHM) with cutoff near 1.65 GHz consistent with ECMI, B* ≈ 0.59 kG; non-detection (3σ) four hours later indicates intermittent/rotationally modulated beamed emission; no unambiguous rotation period recovered; spectroscopy confirms active chromosphere with double-peaked Hα (44.6 km/s separation) from optically thick self-absorption.
AI.conclusion: Coordinated time-series optical photometry, high-resolution spectroscopy, and high-cadence spectropolarimetric radio imaging enable direct probing of coherent radio emission and magnetic activity in nearby M dwarfs.

title: Maximising the Open Magnetic Flux of a Star
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We consider how to distribute the magnetic flux on a star's surface in order to maximise the proportion of open magnetic flux predicted by the potential field source surface model. The proportion of open flux is shown to be maximised by concentrating all of the positive and negative flux at antipodal points. For a typical source surface height, this enhances the open flux by 35% compared to a dipolar distribution. Even if the flux is spread over finite polar caps -- as on the Sun around Solar Minimum -- the open flux is still substantially enhanced compared to the dipole. Nevertheless, we show that the dipole approximation over-estimates the open flux for this kind of flux distribution.

AI.tldr: Concentrating stellar surface magnetic flux at antipodal points maximizes open flux in the potential field source surface model, boosting it by ~35% over a dipole.
AI.motivation: To determine how the spatial distribution of magnetic flux on a star's surface affects the fraction of open magnetic flux predicted by the potential field source surface (PFSS) model.
AI.method: An optimization/analytical study within the PFSS framework, comparing open-flux fractions for different surface flux distributions, including fully concentrated antipodal point sources, finite polar caps (Sun-like at Solar Minimum), and a pure dipole.
AI.result: Open flux is maximized when all positive and negative flux is concentrated at antipodal points; for a typical source surface height this yields ~35% more open flux than a dipolar distribution. Finite polar cap distributions also substantially enhance open flux relative to a dipole. The dipole approximation, however, over-estimates open flux for such flux distributions.
AI.conclusion: Surface flux concentration strongly controls open flux magnitude; antipodal concentration is optimal, and the dipole approximation is inadequate—over-estimating open flux—for realistic cap-type distributions.

title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
comment: published online by Nature on Nov. 18, 2026 (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11221-z)
summary: The formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars. This is theorized to happen via Common Envelope Evolution (CEE), when the stars orbit in a loosely bound, shared convective envelope, triggering an inspiral due to frictional drag. However, this inspiral in such a system has never been observed directly. Here, we present observations of AT 2025abao, a transient eruption in the Andromeda Galaxy, that originates from the CEE of a ~7M$_{\odot}$ asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star with its companion. Extensive pre- and post-eruption spectroscopy is best explained as a ~0.7M$_{\odot}$ companion inspiraling within the convective AGB envelope that powers a seven year period of gradual brightening - the first direct observations of frictional drag energy dissipation induced by CEE. The subsequent merger of the companion with the primary core within a few (<10) orbits powers the ejection of the outermost ~10% of the stellar envelope at speeds ~10x the primary escape speed, and empirically constrains the fraction of dissipated orbital energy available to unbind the convective common envelope, $0.01\lesssim α\lesssim 0.4$. This end-to-end characterization using multi-survey observations demonstrates a path towards mapping the landscape of CEE outcomes with upcoming surveys.

AI.tldr: Observations of AT 2025abao in Andromeda provide the first direct evidence of frictional-drag inspiral during Common Envelope Evolution, a ~0.7 M☉ companion spiraling inside a ~7 M☉ AGB envelope over seven years before merging with the core and ejecting the outer envelope, empirically constraining the envelope-binding efficiency to 0.01 ≲ α ≲ 0.4.
AI.motivation: Compact stellar binaries require rapid orbital tightening, theoretically achieved through Common Envelope Evolution (CEE), in which frictional drag drives inspiral within a shared convective envelope. This inspiral phase had never been directly observed, leaving the physics of CEE—particularly the efficiency with which dissipated orbital energy unbinds the envelope—poorly constrained empirically.
AI.method: Multi-survey observations of the transient AT 2025abao in the Andromeda Galaxy, including extensive pre- and post-eruption spectroscopy, interpreted against a model of a low-mass companion inspiraling within the convective envelope of an AGB primary.
AI.result: The transient is best explained by a ~0.7 M☉ companion spiraling inside the convective envelope of a ~7 M☉ AGB star, producing a seven-year gradual brightening—the first direct observation of frictional drag energy dissipation in CEE. The companion then merges with the primary core within <10 orbits, ejecting the outermost ~10% of the envelope at ~10x the primary escape speed. This yields an empirical constraint on the energy available to unbind the envelope: 0.01 ≲ α ≲ 0.4.
AI.conclusion: The end-to-end characterization of AT 2025abao demonstrates that multi-survey observations can trace CEE from inspiral through merger and ejection, providing a template for mapping the landscape of CEE outcomes with upcoming surveys.

title: Subsequent Dust-Fading Events of the Wolf-Rayet Star WR 59: A Continuous Visual Record
comment: 43 pages, 26 figures, 21 tables. Presents 9 years of unblended visual monitoring of WR 59 (2017-2026), including master chronological logs, high-density intra-night runs, light curves, and TESS space-based overlays. Summary report to appear in the British Astronomical Association Variable Star Section (BAA VSS) Circular No. 211, March 1, 2027
summary: This paper presents long-term visual and space-based monitoring of the WC9d Wolf-Rayet star WR 59 from 2017 to 2026, documenting a profound physical transition from a stable baseline to an ongoing phase of continuous dust production. Visual observations using a 22-inch telescope initially established a four-year quiescent baseline at magnitude 13.9. Following the historic May 2021 discovery fade to magnitude 15.2, long-term nightly visual monitoring documented an accelerating sequence of twelve distinct fading episodes over subsequent years, characterised by progressively shorter inter-fade recovery intervals. Due to severe pixel crowding and flux contamination from a close 11.7 V companion star 11 arcseconds away, automated large-pixel survey pipelines remain completely blind to these high-amplitude fading events. Direct comparisons with NASA's TESS satellite photometry during quiet phases show that targeted visual magnitude estimates measure systemic baseline micro-variations with professional accuracy while bridging space mission coverage gaps. High-density observation blocks during the minimum floor reveal a highly dynamic, rapid, minute-by-minute bimodal oscillation and sub-minute flickering between magnitudes 15.0 and 15.2. At the time of writing, the system remains locked in an unprecedented deep minimum, varying between magnitudes 15.0 and 15.2 for a sustained period exceeding 102 consecutive days. Intensive visual monitoring is ongoing to record the eventual egress recovery profile.

AI.tldr: Long-term visual and TESS-assisted monitoring of WR 59 (2017–2026) reveals a transition from a stable 13.9 mag baseline to continuous dust production, with twelve accelerating fading episodes and an ongoing >102-day deep minimum at 15.0–15.2 mag featuring rapid bimodal oscillations.
AI.motivation: Large-pixel automated survey pipelines are blind to WR 59's high-amplitude fading events due to pixel crowding and flux contamination from a nearby 11.7 V companion 11 arcseconds away, so a dedicated long-term monitoring campaign is needed to characterize the star's variability and dust-production behavior.
AI.method: Nightly visual photometry with a 22-inch telescope from 2017 to 2026, establishing a four-year quiescent baseline, plus direct comparison with NASA TESS satellite photometry during quiet phases and high-density observation blocks during the minimum.
AI.result: A 13.9 mag quiescent baseline was established, followed by the May 2021 fade to 15.2 mag and twelve distinct fading episodes with progressively shorter recovery intervals. Targeted visual estimates matched TESS precision and bridged mission coverage gaps. During the minimum, rapid minute-by-minute bimodal oscillation and sub-minute flickering between 15.0 and 15.2 mag were observed, with the system locked in an unprecedented deep minimum exceeding 102 consecutive days.
AI.conclusion: WR 59 has transitioned from a stable state to continuous dust production with accelerating episodic fades, currently in a record deep minimum; targeted visual monitoring offers professional-grade accuracy for contaminated fields and complements space-based photometry, with intensive monitoring ongoing to capture the egress recovery profile.

title: Multifrequency deep radio continuum VLA observations toward OMC-2/3
summary: We present multiwavelength (0.7-5 cm) Very Large Array continuum observations of high sensitivity (3 $μ$Jy beam$^{-1}$), reaching an angular resolution of $0.4''$ (154 au) toward the Integral Shaped Filament in Orion. We image a field of $12.5'$ in diameter, containing the whole OMC-2 region and the southernmost $2.5'$ of OMC-3. We report the positions, flux densities and spectral indices of 47 radio sources, and discuss their nature. We conclude that, out of the 57 radio sources in the field of view, 36 (63%) are very likely tracing YSOs, 4 are tracing jet/outflow knots, and 6 are extragalactic sources; the nature of the remaining sources is unclear. We identify the driving sources of the 9 previously reported molecular outflows in our field of view. Four of them show a clear elongated radio jet morphology. We detect free-free emission from two potential photoevaporating discs associated with Class III YSOs. We find variability in 11 radio sources, 7 of which are also variable at shorter wavelengths. We find 7 pairs of radio sources with projected separations of 150-3000 au, which are potential binary systems; we identify a total of 17 potential multiple systems within this separation range when taking into account sources detected at other wavelengths. This work highlights the potential of deep VLA observations to uncover a large population of weak radio sources and study their diversity, serving as a guide for future surveys with the SKA and ngVLA.

AI.tldr: Deep 0.7–5 cm VLA imaging of the Orion Integral Shaped Filament detects 57 radio sources, classifying 36 as likely YSOs and characterizing jets, disc emission, variability, and candidate multiple systems.
AI.motivation: Weak radio continuum emission provides a dust-unbiased probe of young stellar objects, jets, and photoevaporating discs, but a large population of faint sources has remained underexplored; deep observations are needed to characterize source diversity and to guide future SKA/ngVLA surveys.
AI.method: Multiwavelength (0.7–5 cm) VLA continuum observations with 3 μJy beam⁻¹ sensitivity and 0.4'' (154 au) resolution over a 12.5' field covering OMC-2 and the southern 2.5' of OMC-3; measurement of positions, flux densities, and spectral indices for 47 radio sources, with classification and cross-matching to outflows and other-wavelength data.
AI.result: Of 57 radio sources in the field, 36 (63%) are very likely YSOs, 4 are jet/outflow knots, and 6 are extragalactic; the remainder are unclassified. Driving sources are identified for all 9 previously known molecular outflows, 4 showing elongated radio jet morphology. Free–free emission is detected from two candidate photoevaporating discs around Class III YSOs. Variability is found in 11 sources (7 also variable at shorter wavelengths), and 7 radio pairs with 150–3000 au separations are identified, yielding 17 potential multiple systems overall.
AI.conclusion: Deep VLA continuum surveys can uncover and classify a large population of faint radio sources in star-forming regions, revealing jets, disc emission, variability, and multiplicity; the results provide a template for future SKA and ngVLA studies.

title: Sun-like stars show lowered X-ray activity together with over-rotation at beyond-solar ages
comment: Accepted for publication by Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: In recent years, substructure in the age-rotation relationship of cool, sun-like stars has been identified, showing deviations from the historical Skumanich law. Since magnetic activity is expected to be the physical root cause of the stellar spin-down, namely via the magnetic braking process mediated through stellar winds, changes in spin-down should correspond to unusual activity behaviour. We selected a sample of old sun-like stars in the solar neighborhood with asteroseismic age estimates and measured rotation periods, and present an analysis of their magnetic activity using deep X-ray observations from XMM-Newton. We observe that sample stars less massive than the Sun (late-G and early-K) agree well with the established rotation-activity relationship, while early-G and late-F stars with masses above solar tend to be unusually X-ray dim for their rotation period. The latter stars rotate faster than same-colour stars in the solar-age open cluster M67, despite being older than M67. Those stars are characterized by either low metallicity ([Fe/H]$\approx -0.2$ dex compared to solar) or by a mix of low coronal temperatures ($< 1.5$ million K) and very low X-ray surface fluxes ($\lesssim 10^4$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$). We conclude that there is sufficient dynamo activity for coronal emission in the sample stars, since we successfully detect the majority of them in our X-ray observations. We argue that stars with extremely low coronal temperature and/or low X-ray flux through the stellar surface may produce an inefficient spin-down through hampered angular momentum shedding. If this is indeed the cause for their over-rotation, the onset age of this effect would need to be at an age of approximately 3~Gyr. However, this behaviour is at odds with studies of stars in the open cluster M67 with a cluster age of $\sim4$ Gyr, which do not show a faster-rotating population of sun-like stars.

AI.tldr: Old sun-like stars more massive than the Sun and either metal-poor or with very cool, weak coronae appear X-ray dim and over-rotating relative to their asteroseismic age, suggesting inefficient magnetic braking possibly beginning near ~3 Gyr — though this conflicts with M67 (age ~4 Gyr) showing no fast-rotating sun-like population.
AI.motivation: Substructure in the age-rotation relation of cool sun-like stars deviates from the classical Skumanich law. Because magnetic braking via winds is the physical driver of spin-down, any anomalous rotation should be mirrored by anomalous magnetic activity; the authors test whether X-ray activity diagnostics can explain the observed rotation substructure.
AI.method: Sample of old, solar-neighbourhood sun-like stars with asteroseismic ages and measured rotation periods. Magnetic activity characterized with deep XMM-Newton X-ray observations: coronal temperatures, X-ray surface fluxes, and comparison against the rotation-activity relation, plus comparison to solar-colour stars in the open cluster M67.
AI.result: Stars below solar mass (late-G, early-K) follow the established rotation-activity relation. Early-G/late-F stars above solar mass are unusually X-ray dim for their rotation period and rotate faster than same-colour M67 stars despite being older. These stars show either low metallicity ([Fe/H] ≈ −0.2 dex) or a mix of low coronal temperature (<1.5 MK) and very low X-ray surface flux (≲10^4 erg s^-1 cm^-2). Dynamo activity is nonetheless sufficient for coronal emission, as most targets are detected.
AI.conclusion: Extremely low coronal temperature and/or low X-ray surface flux may indicate hampered angular-momentum shedding and thus inefficient spin-down, potentially explaining the over-rotation; this effect would have to onset at ~3 Gyr. This is at odds with M67 (~4 Gyr), which lacks a faster-rotating sun-like population.

title: Welopō'ai: A peculiar triple system 8 pc from the Sun
comment: 22 pages, 12 figures, 10 tables. Published in A&A
summary: Context. We report the serendipitous discovery of a white dwarf companion to the M4 V dwarf Welopo'ai Aa (IRAS 21500+5903) during a radial-velocity search for exoplanets with SPIRou. The system is located at 8.46 pc and forms a hierarchical triple with a more distant white dwarf, which has no known analogue within 30 pc. Aims. We characterise the orbital architecture and component masses through a joint Keplerian fit of radial velocities and astrometry, derive the physical parameters of the M dwarf and both white dwarfs, and discuss the implications for common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple dynamics. Methods. We obtained radial velocity measurements with SPIRou spread over 4.8 yr, revealing a large-amplitude signal ($\sim$16 km/s peak-to-peak) that is inconsistent with planetary companions. Follow-up speckle imaging with 'Alopeke at Gemini North and near-infrared (NIR) imaging with GNIRS confirmed a white dwarf companion at sub-arcsecond separation. Results. The system comprises an inner binary with a semi-major axis of $4.644 \pm 0.017$ au ($P \approx 9.83$ yr), consisting of the primary M4 V ($M = 0.4189^{+0.0073}_{-0.0072} M_\odot$) and a white dwarf companion ($M = 0.6180^{+0.0046}_{-0.0045} M_\odot$, $T_{\rm eff} \sim 5210 \pm 320$ K, cooling age 5.3-5.5 Gyr). This inner pair lies at a projected separation of 123.9 au ($P > 1000$ yr) from a previously known white dwarf. The dynamically determined mass of the inner white dwarf is one of only a handful of such measurements for white dwarfs within 20 pc, and the most precise, at the sub-percent (0.7%) level. Conclusions. This system is the closest known triple containing multiple white dwarfs and offers direct dynamical constraints on common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple stability. Furthermore, a tentative near-infrared (IR) excess towards the inner white dwarf further hints at circumstellar dust.

AI.tldr: Serendipitous SPIRou radial-velocity monitoring revealed a white dwarf companion to the M4 V dwarf Welopo'ai Aa (IRAS 21500+5903) at 8.46 pc, forming a hierarchical triple with a second, more distant white dwarf; the system yields a sub-percent dynamical mass for the inner white dwarf.
AI.motivation: During an exoplanet RV search with SPIRou, a large-amplitude (~16 km/s peak-to-peak) signal was found for the nearby M4 V dwarf Welopo'ai Aa, incompatible with a planetary companion and implying a stellar-mass (likely compact) secondary. The system is close (8.46 pc) and has no known analogue within 30 pc, motivating a full characterization of its orbital architecture, component masses, and implications for common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple dynamics.
AI.method: SPIRou radial velocities over 4.8 yr were combined with astrometry in a joint Keplerian fit to derive orbital elements and dynamical masses. Follow-up speckle imaging with 'Alopeke at Gemini North and NIR imaging with GNIRS confirmed the sub-arcsecond white dwarf companion. Physical parameters of the M dwarf and both white dwarfs were derived, including effective temperature and cooling age of the inner white dwarf.
AI.result: The inner binary has a = 4.644 ± 0.017 au (P ≈ 9.83 yr), with the M4 V primary at 0.4189 (+0.0073/−0.0072) M☉ and a white dwarf companion at 0.6180 (+0.0046/−0.0045) M☉, T_eff ≈ 5210 ± 320 K, and cooling age 5.3–5.5 Gyr. This inner pair orbits at a projected separation of 123.9 au (P > 1000 yr) from a previously known white dwarf. The inner white dwarf mass is one of only a handful of dynamical measurements within 20 pc and the most precise, at the 0.7% (sub-percent) level. A tentative NIR excess toward the inner white dwarf hints at circumstellar dust.
AI.conclusion: This is the closest known triple system containing multiple white dwarfs, providing direct dynamical constraints on common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple stability, plus a possible dust reservoir around the inner white dwarf.

title: Infrared spectrum of the Type Iax supernova remnant Pa30
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 8 pages, 4 figures
summary: The central star of Pa30 and its nebulosity offer one of the best opportunities to study a SN Iax explosion and its remnant. Pa30 is thought to be the product of the historical supernova explosion of 1181. No infrared spectroscopy of its extremely hot central star has hitherto been reported. Here, we present a 0.75-5 $μ$m spectrum taken by the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx), together with ground-based infrared spectra, at higher resolution, covering the 0.8-2.5 $μ$m region. The spectra contain very broad lines, which we have attempted to identify and model using the codes CMFGEN and CLOUDY. The CMFGEN modelling suggests that most of the lines are due to OVI. However, CLOUDY modelling, using expected theoretical abundances for the bound remnants of SN Iax explosions, provides evidence for the presence of coronal lines of Si, S, Mg, and Al arising from a shocked gas. This strengthens the suggestion that Pa30 is indeed the remnant of a SN Iax explosion.

AI.tldr: We present the first infrared spectroscopy (0.75–5 μm SPHEREx plus ground-based 0.8–2.5 μm spectra) of Pa30's hot central star, identifying very broad lines via CMFGEN and CLOUDY modelling and finding coronal Si, S, Mg, and Al lines from shocked gas that support Pa30 as a SN Iax remnant.
AI.motivation: Pa30 and its nebula are among the best laboratories for studying a SN Iax explosion and its remnant, being plausibly the product of the historical 1181 supernova; however, no infrared spectroscopy of its extremely hot central star had previously been reported.
AI.method: A 0.75–5 μm spectrum obtained with SPHEREx, combined with higher-resolution ground-based infrared spectra covering 0.8–2.5 μm. The very broad lines are identified and modelled with the stellar-atmosphere code CMFGEN and the photoionization code CLOUDY, the latter adopting expected theoretical abundances for bound remnants of SN Iax explosions.
AI.result: CMFGEN modelling suggests most of the broad lines originate from O VI. In contrast, CLOUDY modelling with SN Iax remnant abundances provides evidence for coronal lines of Si, S, Mg, and Al arising from shocked gas.
AI.conclusion: The detection of coronal lines from shocked gas strengthens the suggestion that Pa30 is indeed the remnant of a SN Iax explosion.

title: Asteroseismology of AI Velorum: a prototype of high-amplitude delta Scuti stars
comment: 15 pages, 12 figures, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary:
AI Velorum is exceptional among high-amplitude δScuti (HADS) stars because of its multimode pulsations. Despite being an excellent target for asteroseismology, this prototype star has not been studied in detail.
  We determine the stellar parameters, age, and evolutionary stage of AI Vel, constrain envelope convection and convective core overshooting, and test three opacity data sets: OPAL, OP, and OPLIB.
  We analysed TESS photometry, ground-based Strömgren photometry, and HARPS spectroscopy. Modes were identified using photometric and spectroscopic methods, and empirical values of the non-adiabatic f-parameter were derived for both radial modes. Seismic modelling was performed within a Bayesian framework supported by Monte Carlo simulations.
  We confirm the radial nature of the two dominant modes and identify one non-radial mode as most likely an axisymmetric dipole or quadrupole mode. Within the explored parameter space, only OPAL models reproduce the observed position of AI Vel in the HR diagram, whereas OP and OPLIB models are too cool and underluminous. All seismic models favour inefficient envelope convection (mixing-length parameter alpha_{mlt}\lesssim 0.5). Including the non-radial mode substantially reduces the formal posterior uncertainties, but the ambiguity in its identification introduces additional model-dependent uncertainties. AI Vel is an evolved, slowly rotating star in the hydrogen shell-burning phase.
  Our results demonstrate the diagnostic power of combining pulsation frequencies with empirical f-parameters. The preference for OPAL opacities is consistent with results for several other HADS and SX Phoenicis stars but does not imply a general superiority of OPAL opacities.

AI.tldr: This study derives stellar parameters, age, and evolutionary stage of the HADS star AI Velorum and tests envelope convection, core overshooting, and three opacity tables (OPAL, OP, OPLIB) via asteroseismic modelling of TESS, Strömgren, and HARPS data.
AI.motivation: AI Vel is a prototype multimode HADS star and an ideal asteroseismology target, yet has not been studied in detail despite its exceptional multimode pulsation.
AI.method: Combined TESS photometry, ground-based Strömgren photometry, and HARPS spectroscopy; mode identification via photometric and spectroscopic methods; empirical non-adiabatic f-parameters for both radial modes; Bayesian seismic modelling supported by Monte Carlo simulations across OPAL, OP, and OPLIB opacities.
AI.result: The two dominant modes are confirmed radial; one non-radial mode is most likely an axisymmetric dipole or quadrupole mode. Only OPAL models reproduce AI Vel's observed HR-diagram position, while OP and OPLIB models are too cool and underluminous. All seismic models favor inefficient envelope convection (alpha_mlt ≲ 0.5). Including the non-radial mode reduces formal posterior uncertainties but adds model-dependent uncertainty from mode ambiguity. AI Vel is evolved, slowly rotating, and in the hydrogen shell-burning phase.
AI.conclusion: Combining pulsation frequencies with empirical f-parameters has strong diagnostic power. The preference for OPAL opacities agrees with results for other HADS and SX Phoenicis stars but does not imply general superiority of OPAL.
